headline: Daily research brief — Monday, October 19

items.detail: Tesla reports Wed Oct 21 after the close with the single steepest event hump on the board: front-expiry (Oct 23) ATM implied volatility at 0.687 against 0.443 thirty days out, and the straddle implying ±6.41% against an 8-quarter realized-reaction average of 7.77% — the only watchlist name priced below its own history. Four of the last eight reactions were up and four down (range −14.5% to +21.9%), so direction is a coin flip with the widest tail on the desk. Premium into this binary is an avoid.
items.title: TSLA Wednesday is the week's defining event — the market prices less than history delivered

items.detail: The Nov 6 straddle (first expiry after the Nov 2 print) implies ±5.31% against an 8-quarter realized average of 2.46%, and six of eight prints were down-but-small. Premium is rich on realized history unless the Jul-26 print (−7.35%, the largest in the sample) marks a genuine volatility-regime shift in AAPL reactions rather than an outlier — only subsequent prints will tell. MSFT's Oct 28 setup is roughly in line (implied ±5.61% vs 7.02% realized).
items.title: AAPL's event premium is ~2.2× its own history — the clearest mispricing signal on the board

items.detail: SPY's 30-day ATM IV of 14.25% sits 5.3 percentage points above trailing 20-day realized 9.0%, with normal upward term-structure slope, no event hump, and no earnings anywhere near — the only verdict that is not window-contingent. QQQ, AAPL, MSFT, and TSLA verdicts all rest on jump days that drive more than 30% of realized variance. NVDA's +15.6pp spread is arithmetic, not a mispricing: Nov-18 earnings sit inside the Nov-20 expiry. IV rank is unverified for all six names — richness is judged on the IV-minus-realized proxy only.
items.title: SPY is the only clean event-free rich-premium read

items.detail: FRED (Oct 16 observations): fed funds effective 3.88% (mid-range of 3.75–4.00%), 10Y at 5.09% — 22bp off the Oct 5 local high of 5.31%, so relief without a regime change. 2s10s flattened 50bp to +35bp over 60 days; SOFR equals fed funds, so funding plumbing is normal. Chair Warsh refused to signal the October decision at the Oct 16 IMF meeting, and September minutes show most participants see another hike likely by year-end. September core CPI ran +2.6% vs 2.5% expected, supporting the hike case; the headline year-over-year number is unverified at the single-number level (secondaries disagree). Oct 28 is a policy-event risk for rate-sensitive premium, not a priced-in certainty.
items.title: Rates: 10Y 5.09% headwind persists but is no longer intensifying; the Oct 27–28 FOMC is live and unpriced
